THE WHOLE dev_storyflow FLEET LOG TRIAGED: 6,203 lines, 62 entries, 4 Aug-3-to-Aug-15. Roughly 28 fixed, 26 open, the rest partial. The high-severity ones were verified against the running code; the tail was classified with less depth and that is marked.

⚠️ I TRIAGED A STALE COPY FIRST AND ANTHONY CAUGHT IT. I worked through a 122 KB upload from Aug 8 and reported it as complete; the current file is 658 KB — my triage covered the first 19%. HIS RULE, now standing: dev_storyflow feedback is ONE APPEND-ONLY FILE, so only the newest upload matters and every older copy is a prefix. VERIFIED rather than taken on trust: the 754-line copy is a byte-identical prefix of the 6,203-line one, so the earlier triage stands for those entries and only the remainder needed work. THIRD stale-or-misidentified-document error of the session; the first two I caught, this one I did not.

⭐⭐ THREE OF THEIR AUGUST 15 REPORTS WERE FIXED TODAY, BY ME, WITHOUT KNOWING THEY HAD BEEN FILED — and two shipped as their asks VERBATIM:
• `propose_heal` naming one of four Projects as `target_id` while sweeping globally → fixed in #210, which added `scope`, `projects_in_scope`.
• `propose_heal` unable to distinguish "no bad merges" from "no candidates at all" — their idea (1) was `merge_candidates_considered: 0 alongside operations: []`, and that is the field name that shipped. Their framing is the better one and belongs in the record: "the difference between a check that PASSED and a check that COULD NOT FAIL".
• `answer_question` rejecting both ids `open_questions` had just handed them → fixed in #201; the request now reads "either this or `question_id` — whichever you have in hand", which is their idea (1).

ALSO VERIFIED FIXED, against code rather than changelog: `set_verification_status` SILENTLY DELETING `last_run_at` when the parameter was omitted — their 🚨 RETEST on v0.26.1, the data-loss one — is fixed at `verify.rs:167`, which now replaces it only when supplied. The `check-health`-named-first string (filed FOUR times across two days by three seats, with a fleet-wide stop-order) fixed in #102. The accountability edge they measured as islanding 109 nodes, and which ANTHONY HIMSELF relayed as "reflow2 has two of the three WHO axes and is missing the third", shipped as `OWNED_BY` — though reflow2's own graph uses it ZERO times. `append_only`/`living` volatility shipped, including the sub-thread where the reporter corrected their own entry and then RETRACTED the correction as also wrong.

⭐ THE OPEN ONE THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ME TODAY: `set_artifact_checksum` accepts a 13-character digest without complaint, and is one-shot so a bad baseline is easy to write and hard to correct. `canonical_checksum` still takes any hex string of length ≤ 64. Their second case — "a digest I had TYPED FROM MEMORY rather than read from `sha256sum`", well-formed and simply WRONG — is EXACTLY the error I made this afternoon writing a fabricated checksum into `art:schema-build`. Their ask (1), a one-line shape guard, would have caught their first case; nothing catches the second, and they say so.

THE OTHER OPEN ONES WORTH RANKING:
1. A LOST UPDATE ON THE SHARED GRAPH, OBSERVED FROM BOTH SIDES. `create_node` has no expected-current-value parameter, so no write can be made conditional on what was read; `claim_region` is advisory and nothing consults it. The winner was never told. "Every property edit is a lost update waiting to happen, and detection is left to luck." PARTIALLY mitigated since: `create_node` now returns a `revision` block naming what it replaced — which is detection after the fact, not prevention.
2. RE-USING AN EXISTING NODE ID IN AN INGEST PASS IS A WRITE, NOT A REFERENCE, and there is no cite-only form. A worker silently reverted a USER-RULED restoration with their next batch — on the one node the fleet was already watching, which they had personally restored thirty minutes earlier.
3. ZERO-DEGREE NODES ARE NOT REPORTED. Both their packages had a baseline DesignEpoch with no edges at all, through every `detect_defects` and `loop_status` call, one of them answering `clean: true`. `heal.rs:879` covers Decisions only. Their second half is sharper: `disconnected_community` computes MODULARITY but its words claim UNREACHABILITY, so it invites the wrong repair and missed the genuinely unreachable node.
4. `orphan_node` FIRES ON THE STATE A DISPOSITION RULE PRESCRIBES — a document deliberately registered with no claims. Their defect count moved 88 → 97 across ten correct writes, with 31 more owed. "The disposition rule and the defect detector make each other unreadable, and the correct action degrades the instrument."

THE REST, classified but not individually re-verified: a Capability cannot say WHICH implementation it describes; `get_node` returns properties and no edges; `VIOLATES_RULE` is declared and never offered by `describe_schema` (0 uses here); a `RISKS` edge predicted a live incident and no routine call surfaces it (1 use here); the duplicate scorer landing a true pair and an unrelated pair on the same score; `ingest-corpus`'s `fragment_id` rule colliding with existing id conventions; `describe_schema` costing ~15k tokens to answer what properties a type has; and `add_change_event` being unable to record an addition in advance.

⭐ WHAT THE FILE IS, beyond a bug list: a fleet instrumenting its own tooling under real load, with a no-consolidation rule that earns its keep — the same defect filed four times by three seats is what shows a tool doing it to everyone rather than one seat's opinion. Two entries are the reporter correcting themselves and then retracting the correction, in public, which is a standard of honesty worth matching.
